name: apify
description: Run Apify Actors and read their results: web scraping, browsing and data extraction for agents
long_description: Bring an Apify API token; the gateway keeps it off your Sprite and sends it as a bearer token. Saving, replacing or testing the token reads the account it belongs to (GET /v2/users/me), which costs nothing. A Sprite can then run any Actor or saved task (waiting for the result, or starting a run and polling it), abort its own runs, read the datasets and key-value store records runs produce, and search Apify Store for Actors. Runs use your Apify platform credits and, for paid Actors, the Actor's own price. Token, account, billing, webhook, schedule and Actor-management endpoints are not forwarded, so a Sprite cannot create, change or delete Actors, tasks, schedules or webhooks.

examples.title: Read a web page as Markdown with RAG Web Browser (uses your Apify credits)
notes: Returns the dataset items directly: `[{"metadata": {"url", "title"}, "markdown": "..."}]`. A `query` that isn't a URL runs a Google search and reads the top `maxResults` pages.

examples.title: Check pages for prompt injection before an agent trusts them (Page Court)
notes: Replace ACTOR_ID with the Actor's id or `username~page-court`. Any Actor runs the same way.

examples.title: Start a run without waiting; replace ACTOR_ID
notes: Returns `data.id` (the run) and `data.defaultDatasetId`. Poll `GET /v2/actor-runs/RUN_ID?waitForFinish=60` until `data.status` is `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED`, `ABORTED` or `TIMED-OUT`.

examples.title: Read a run's status; replace RUN_ID
Read a dataset's items; replace DATASET_ID
Read a run's OUTPUT record; replace STORE_ID
Read the account the token belongs to

messages.400: Apify rejected the request (%{status}); check error.message, often the Actor's input
messages.402: Not enough Apify credits, or the Actor needs a paid plan; check console.apify.com/billing
messages.403: The Apify token can't do this; it may be scoped to other Actors or storages
messages.404: No such Actor, task, run or storage, or the token can't see it
messages.408: The run didn't finish in time; start it with POST /v2/acts/ACTOR_ID/runs and poll it instead
messages.429: Apify rate limit reached; wait for the Retry-After header and retry
messages.provider_unreachable: Could not reach Apify; retry later

presentation.tagline: Run Apify Actors and read their results from a Sprite without putting your Apify token on it.
presentation.setup: Sign in at console.apify.com, open Settings, then API & Integrations, and copy a personal API token (it starts with `apify_api_`). For least privilege, create a scoped token limited to the Actors and storages the Sprite needs. The free plan includes a monthly credit.

notices.title: Billing
notices.body: Saving or testing the token reads `GET /v2/users/me` and costs nothing. Every Actor run uses Apify platform credits for its compute and proxies, and paid Actors also charge their own price per run, per result or per event. Reading datasets, records, runs and Apify Store is free.

notices.title: Scope
notices.body: Only these are forwarded: reading the token's account, searching Apify Store, reading an Actor, running Actors and saved tasks (`/runs`, `/run-sync`, `/run-sync-get-dataset-items`), reading and aborting runs and their logs, and reading datasets and key-value store records. Token, account, billing, webhook, schedule and Actor- or task-management endpoints are not, and nothing can be written to storages directly.

usage_notes: The gateway waits up to 120 seconds for an answer, and `run-sync` endpoints wait for the run to finish. Add `?timeout=100` (seconds) so a slow run stops before the gateway gives up, or start the run with `POST /v2/acts/ACTOR_ID/runs` and poll `GET /v2/actor-runs/RUN_ID?waitForFinish=60`.
Actor ids are `username~actor-name` (the `~` replaces the `/` of the Store name) or the Actor's 17-character id. Task ids work the same way.
Error bodies are `{"error": {"type": "...", "message": "..."}}`. A run that fails still answers 201 when started; check `data.status` and the log.
Standby Actors answer on their own hosts, which this connector doesn't cover; run them through `/run-sync` instead.
